1. (Currently amended) A method of cementing comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin __derived from chicory__; placing the cement composition in a subterranean formation; and allowing the cement composition to set.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 2 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F __and the carboxylated inulin functions as a biodegradable retarder__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed __due to the biodegradable retarder properties of the carboxylated inulin__.

4. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 2 wt.% of the cement composition.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 500 or higher __and is processed from chicory__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin __derived from chicory inulin__.

8. (Original) The method of claim 7 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.3.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.1 to about 5 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an al pha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a subterranean formation __at a depth greater than 5,000 feet__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore __at a temperature exceeding 200°F__.

13. (Currently amended) A method of cementing in a subterranean formation comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin __derived from chicory__; placing the cement composition in the subterranean formation; and allowing the cement composition to set therein.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 2 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F __and the carboxylated inulin functions as a biodegradable retarder__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed __due to the biodegradable retarder properties of the carboxylated inulin__.

16. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition.

17. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 2 wt.% of the cement composition.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 500 or higher __and is processed from chicory__.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises carboxymethylated inulin __derived from chicory inulin__.

20. (Original) The method of claim 19 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethylated of from about 0.1 to about 0.3.

21. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.1 to about 5 wt. % of carboxylated inulin.

22. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore __at a temperature exceeding 200°F__.
